references.text: The first time acacia wood (עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים) is mentioned as a building material for the tabernacle, here for the ark of the covenant.
Acacia wood is listed among the materials the Israelites were to gather for the construction of the tabernacle.
Detailed instructions on placing the boards (הַקְּרָשִׁים) of the tabernacle.
Fulfillment of the command: Bezalel made upright boards of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Acacia wood is also used to build the altar of burnt offering, showing consistent use of this material in the tabernacle.
The incense altar was also to be made of acacia wood, the same material as the boards of the tabernacle.
Moses made an ark of acacia wood, showing the continued use of this material for holy objects.
Complementary instructions on the construction of the tabernacle: the arrangement of the boards and the function of the crossbars to bind them together.
Fulfillment reference: Confirmation that the crossbars for binding the boards were made exactly as instructed.
Fulfillment reference: Historical confirmation that the instruction to make the boards for the south side was completed.
